output.title: Spot proof-of-concept debt before you sign off on the pilot
output.body:
If you run a 1–10-person business and you have tried ChatGPT but not tied it to a real workflow, this is the point to watch: proof-of-concept debt. That is the work you knowingly leave unfinished in a pilot — missing documentation, an untested edge case, a manual step that still needs a person, or a bug you decide to live with for now.

The mistake is not having deferred work. The mistake is treating every deferred item as if it belongs in the same bucket.

Use one simple checkpoint at pilot close: is this still only a proof, or have you decided it now needs to become part of production? If it is still a proof, keep the deferred items in a separate post-pilot list. If it is now a production candidate, pause expansion until the deferred list is reviewed and scoped properly.

The practical next step is to write three columns before you sign off: what was deferred, why it was deferred, and whether each item is essential before rollout or genuinely post-launch. Review that page with the owner before anyone calls the pilot complete. Keep it as a working record, not a warranty. That small bit of paper saves you from discovering, a week later, that “done” was doing too much work.
